statement: For every grid satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r and r is the maximum possible cardinality of a valid invitation set. A valid invitation set is a set S of ordered pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n such that: (a) grid[i][j] = 1 for every (i,j) in S; (b) no two distinct pairs in S have the same first coordinate; (c) no two distinct pairs in S have the same second coordinate. Thus r = max { |S| : S is a valid invitation set }, where the empty set is allowed and contributes 0.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Assume 1 <= m <= 200, 1 <= n <= 200, every row of grid has length n, and for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: For every grid satisfying the preconditions, maximum_invitations does not fail: it returns a value r of type i64 (no arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic occurs).
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Assume 1 <= m <= 200, 1 <= n <= 200, every row of grid has length n, and for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: If some row i0 with 0 <= i0 < m satisfies grid[i0][j] = 0 for every 0 <= j < n, then whenever the function returns r, r is also the maximum possible number of accepted invitations for the (m-1) x n matrix obtained by deleting row i0 from grid and keeping the other rows in their original relative order. If m = 1, the matrix after deletion has no rows and its maximum possible number is 0.

statement: Let H be any m x n matrix with entries in {0,1} such that grid[i][j] <= H[i][j] for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Whenever the function returns r for grid, r <= M(H), where M(H) is the maximum possible number of accepted invitations for H, meaning the maximum size of a set of pairs (i,j) with H[i][j] = 1, at most one per row, and at most one per column.
